diagnosis: Survivor is roughly breakeven overall (50.7% WR, -$68.37 over 404 trades) but the aggregate masks a bimodal structure: ARB setups are strongly profitable (92% WR, +$5.89 on tiny volume) while the dominant MOMENTUM strategy (383 of 404 trades, 95% of volume) is a net loser (49% WR, -$55.81). Within momentum, the bot is correctly vetoing the worst bucket (move10-20bps, -33.47 PnL, 28/81 win) via lessons, which is working as designed in the recent decision log. However, it continues to enter trades in the 'move<10bps' bucket (-5.55 PnL, 123 trades, 48% WR) and price0.55-0.70 bucket (-7.21 PnL, 84 trades, 51% WR) which are validated as marginally negative but not vetoed. The 'all-agree' peer bucket is actually the worst-performing crowd signal (-18.99 PnL over 112 trades, 44.6% WR) despite intuitively seeming like a strong confirmation signal — this is counterintuitive and suggests peer-agreement is a lagging/contrarian indicator in this market, likely because by the time all coins agree the move is already priced in and mean-reversion kicks in within the 5-min window. DOGE is bleeding badly (39% WR, -$23.45) and should be restricted or dropped. BTC is the only coin with solid edge (60% WR, +$10.83) and should be favored. The left60-120s bucket is a confirmed loser (-20.25 PnL, 35.6% WR) while left120+ is the only profitable time bucket (+10.77 PnL), indicating the bot's current min_entry_left_sec=150 is already near the edge of acceptable entry timing but trades are still slipping into the 60-120s decay zone somehow (likely late entries within the same market cycle or exits that are stop/TP-driven, not fresh entries). Stop-loss trades are notably painful — multiple stop-loss exits at 0.19-0.25 bid on trades entered at 0.55-0.60 ask represent near-max-loss events, and left<60s stop-exits show -1.49 expectancy over just 13 samples (small but alarming). The bot's current edge threshold (min_edge=0.06) and confidence (0.7) are not preventing persistently mediocre momentum entries; the edge calc may be miscalibrated since many 'skip' edges shown (0.03-0.10) don't clearly separate winners from losers in the data. Overall this looks like a strategy with a thin, inconsistent edge that is being correctly pruned by the lesson-veto system but still over-trading on weak signals (small moves, high peer consensus, mid-range prices) that don't carry real predictive power in this 5-minute crypto regime.
